drivingQuestion: What does the Rabbis' 'even the blasphemer' refer to?
outcomeNote: Only the question is posed; the answer lies beyond this unit.

segments.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים אַף הַמְגַדֵּף כּוּ׳. מַאי אַף הַמְגַדֵּף שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה?
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «And the Rabbis say:» The halakha is the same, i.e., there is no obligation to bring a sin offering, «even» with regard to «the one who blasphemes,» as it is stated with regard to the sin offering: “You shall have one law for him who performs the action unwittingly” (Numbers 15:29), excluding one who blasphemes, as he does not perform an action but sins with speech. The Gemara asks: «What» caused the Rabbis to specify: «Even» one who «blasphemes, as he does not perform an action?» Why do the Rabbis mention this explanation?
